pr_title: Math: Make Euler, Quaternion and Color iterable.
pr_body:
Fixed #23793.

**Description**

This PR makes Euler, Quaternion and Color iterable similar to `Vector2`, `Vector3` and `Vector4`.
pr_comments: Euler is not well-defined without a specified `order`. Was omitting it intentional?

> Euler is not well-defined without a specified order. Was omitting it intentional?

I don't think most users are interested in the order property. However, I see now that methods like `toArray()` also honor it. I'll update the PR.

issue_context.title: RFC: Making Euler, Color, Quaternions iterable - and consequently spreadable - like Vector*
issue_context.body:
Vectors are iterable, so they can be spread to an array like `[...vector]`. The same isn't true for Euler, and users ** cough cough me right now ** might expect consistent behaviour.

I was surprised to see this missing, so I'm wondering wether there is a reason we wouldn't make them behave in the same way. 
I know order might be one reason, but then again users could order before spreading.

The code itself would just be the few lines to add the feature and a test, shouldn't take a long time, I'm more interested in why this could be a bad idea.

Have a great weekend and hugs all around!

EDIT: 
- Quaternion
- Color

Are also candidates for this
comments: @LeviPesin also Quaternion. Let me report all of those in the initial comment, it's a good idea

Matrix3/4 also is not iterable, but there is not obvious which order of elements should be returned.
(Currently Matrix.set uses one order, while Matrix.toArray/fromArray uses another, see https://github.com/mrdoob/three.js/issues/23634)
I don't think matrix classes should be iterable.

>I don't think matrix classes should be iterable.

Can you explain why you feel that way?

@Mugen87 the matrix classes already do assume column-major when converting to array ( with the `toArray` method ), so I think this wouldn't be that different.

If a user needs them in row-major they'll transpose themselves - I found myself in that position in the past. We'd be assuming the same level of knowledge for both methods

> Can you explain why you feel that way?

I'm in general no fan of using or promoting matrices in user related workflows. I don't think the engine should guide users towards matrices but to the transformation properties of `Object3D`(position, rotation/quaternion, scale).
But there any many applications of matrices in users' three.js-related code that are not related to the transformation properties of Object3D...
That's true but even then I don't understand why someone wants to iterate over the elements of a matrix.

review_comments:
could you not use this here and the other cases?

```
assert.deepEqual( array, [ 0, 0.5, 1 ] ) 
```

For quaternions either do it like this or keep the long form:

```
var q = new Quaternion( 1, 1, 1 )
var array = [ ...q ]
assert.deepEqual( array.slice( 0, 3 ), [ 1, 1, 1 ] )
assert.strictEqual( array[ 3 ], 3 )
```

Asking this also because I'm curious about preferences regarding this or if there's some related history 👍
I just honored the current approach for comparing arrays to keep the code consistent. Feel free to update the unit tests in a separate PR with your suggestion.
